# Quantum Field Chirality Sensing

> A rotation-invariant test for the sign of three unknown local spin rotations. A sheltered fourth spin makes one-window detection possible. The rare-outcome statistic has a matching weak-exposure sample exponent for fresh independent rounds.

## Scientific account

- [Model and results](science/model.md): Exposure, spin reference, promise, shot and control resources.
- [Sensing protocol](science/protocol.md): Two configurations of a common SWAP and detector, exact chirality contrast, finite sign guarantee and Bernstein bound.
- [Converse](science/converse.md): Exact three-spin blindness and small-time Hellinger bound.
- [Robustness](science/robustness.md): Binary detector floor, routing-dependent bias and imperfect spectator shielding.
- [Two exposures](science/two-exposures.md): One extra coherent sensing window and a cyclic exchange replace the sheltered spin.

## Learn and reproduce

- [Learning route](learning/README.md): Start with the one external reading, connect it to the protocol and work through 30 milestones.
- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): Supplied-state chirality, unknown-gate comparison and experimental primitives.
- [Verification](verification/README.md): Exact finite dimensions, numerical identities and limits of the tests.

The matched rate fixes the field bound and the chirality gap and charges all rounds. It permits classical adaptation across rounds and ideal rotation-invariant quantum operations within a round.
